List the reporting conventions each handler accepts

Source: R/conventions.R
conventions.Rd

Some results depend on a choice the statistics cannot show: which effect size was computed (choices$convention in appendix()) and, for an unbalanced factorial ANOVA, the type of sums of squares (choices$ss_type, also ss_type in sufficient_stats()). conventions() lists the codes reprokit accepts for them. It reads the handler registry, the same place appendix() validates against, so the list cannot drift from the package.

Usage

conventions(handler = NULL)

Arguments

handler

A handler name from handlers(), or NULL for all handlers that accept a convention choice.

Value

A data frame with one row per accepted code and columns handler, choice ("convention" or "ss_type", the name used in choices), code (the exact string reprokit accepts), default (logical) and label (the short label used in the appendix).

Details

default is TRUE for the code reprokit uses when the argument is left out. The sums of squares type has one on the share side: type III, because a fitted aov does not record it, shown in the appendix as reprokit's default, not the author's answer. Checking a paper never assumes a type. An effect-size convention with several codes has no default: leaving it out means "not declared". A handler with a single code (V, w) uses it.

Examples

conventions("t_paired")
#>    handler     choice   code default                                 label
#> 1 t_paired convention    d_z   FALSE           d_z (SD of the differences)
#> 2 t_paired convention   d_rm   FALSE              d_rm (repeated measures)
#> 3 t_paired convention   d_av   FALSE                     d_av (average SD)
#> 4 t_paired convention   g_av   FALSE g_av (average SD, Hedges' correction)
#> 5 t_paired convention   eta2   FALSE                           eta squared
#> 6 t_paired convention omega2   FALSE                         omega squared
subset(conventions(), choice == "ss_type")
#>           handler  choice code default    label
#> 3 anova_factorial ss_type  III    TRUE type III
#> 4 anova_factorial ss_type   II   FALSE  type II
#> 5 anova_factorial ss_type    I   FALSE   type I
